plans.note: Check Article 12 (indemnification/insurance) and the Article 13.6 disclaimer for any cap or consequential-damages waiver; co-development agreements of this type often carry only a disclaimer and no monetary cap, in which case flag as missing after confirming Article 15 miscellaneous contains none.

Article 12 defines PB Indemnified Parties and SFJ Indemnified Parties; assess whether SFJ's indemnity to PB covers third-party IP and SFJ misconduct and whether PB's indemnity (as the operating party running the Clinical Trials) is unusually broad.

Look for Exclusive Period, Competing Product / Brilinta Competing Product and Generic Ticagrelor Product restrictions in the definitions and in the covenants at 7.5.3/7.6 limiting PB's ability to develop or license competing products.

Test whether PB is locked into Approved CRO / Approved Vendor / GMP Manufacturer selections or an Exclusive Period that bars sourcing or licensing elsewhere; note SFJ consent gates in Article 3 and the Article 7 covenants.

No MFN-style pricing or best-terms language is signalled in the outline; check Article 6 payment mechanics and Licensing Transaction definitions before concluding absent, and do not flag an MFN running in our favour.

Employee non-solicit is not evident; scan Article 15 miscellaneous and the confidentiality article for any personnel restriction binding PB before marking missing (rule is presence-based, so absence is acceptable).

Article 14 termination provisions plus the Buy-Out Payment / Approval Buy-Out / Change of Control Buy-Out and Program Transfer mechanics in Articles 6 and 14 determine whether PB can exit and at what cost.
Term runs to Development Term/Completion milestones rather than a renewing subscription term; confirm Article 14 has no auto-extension before recording as not applicable/absent.
Governing law, Dispute escalation to Executive Officers and any arbitration/venue clause should sit in Article 15 miscellaneous; check whether disputes go to courts in an accepted jurisdiction.

Assignment clause expected in Article 15; cross-check the Change of Control definition and the Change of Control Buy-Out Payment in Article 6 / termination rights in Article 14 for penalties triggered by our change of control.

Article 11 governs Intellectual Property and Personally Identifiable Information; verify PB retains Existing PB Intellectual Property, Trial Inventions, Research Results and Clinical Trials Database ownership and that nothing assigns PB data or IP to SFJ.

Review any licence PB grants SFJ and any licence-back or Program Transfer licence for scope, revocability and coverage of Affiliates/Permitted Third Parties; note the AZ License and Existing Licenses definitions as constraints.

Article 9 (Records) and the affirmative covenants in 7.6 are the likely audit/inspection hooks against PB; check notice, frequency, on-site scope and who bears cost, plus any Development Cost audit in Article 4.

Direction check: identify any payment payable by PB that functions as a penalty (Buy-Out Payments, Timeline Remediation Plan consequences, interest or default amounts) as distinguished from SFJ's contingent Approval Payments.

Article 13 representations and warranties plus the 13.6 disclaimer; note that PB is the performing party here, so focus on whether the disclaimer strips warranties we rely on from SFJ and whether PB's warranties exceed the playbook.
Article 12 heading covers Indemnification and Insurance; confirm coverage types/limits and whether the obligation is mutual or one-way on PB as trial sponsor.

Check Development Costs / Maximum Development Costs and PB Costs allocation in Article 4 and the payment obligations in Article 6 for any committed spend or take-or-pay style obligation on PB without an exit.

Program Transfer / Program Transfer Agreement and post-termination effects in Article 14, read with the Clinical Trials Master File and Database provisions in Articles 9 and 11, should cover data return and transition assistance in both directions.
